learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 1.03 times and locked it in before controls opened.
observations.exploration: At 298 K the tail was 1.7 per billion and rate 1.00. Warm to 308 K produced 3.3 and 1.93. Keyboard Home reached 288 K, 0.9 and 0.50; End restored 308 K.
observations.reveal: Explanation corrected the prediction to 1.9 times, tied rate to the tail and stated that doubling per 10 K fits barriers near 50 kJ/mol rather than being a law.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshot inspected. Main distribution, broken horizontal axis and pink barrier tail zoomed 250 million times were visible with dashed baseline; explanatory text fit the card.
observations.previewIsolation: Evaluation preview banner said learning history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviewers judgments were inspected.

prediction.reason: Clear numerical commitment exposes proportional warming intuition.

interaction.reason: Slider creates a meaningful reversible contrast with linked metrics.

payoff.reason: The explanation connects the visible rare tail to the rate correction.
payoff.evidence: 1.7 to 3.3 per billion compared with nearly unchanged crowd.

clarity.reason: Labels explain the barrier and visibly disclose the large tail magnification.
clarity.evidence: Barrier, collision energy axis, axis break and 250 million times zoom shown.

transfer.reason: A conditional rule of thumb is supplied but no new application is attempted.
transfer.evidence: Near 50 kJ/mol qualification accompanies doubling per 10 K.

accessibility.reason: A complete mode audit was not performed.
accessibility.evidence: Keyboard endpoint operation observed; screen reader, contrast and reduced motion not audited.

surprise.reason: Small warming produces an almost doubled rate.

visualExplanation.reason: Magnified tail makes the causal comparison visible.
visualExplanation.evidence: Pink tail and dashed baseline beside nearly unchanged distribution.

playfulness.reason: Exploration is a direct slider experiment.

practicalValue.reason: Helps qualify a common temperature rule.
practicalValue.evidence: Rule explicitly limited to a barrier range.

depth.reason: Relates distribution tails, threshold and rate.
depth.evidence: Barrier around twenty thermal energies explains steep sensitivity.

complexity.reason: A simple slider supports an unfamiliar distribution-tail argument.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Relating a tiny shaded tail to a reaction rate requires distribution and threshold reasoning.
complexity.interfaceBurden: One button and one slider with immediate numbers.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Energy barriers, kelvin and per-billion frequency are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: kJ/mol, multiplicative rates and a broken magnified axis.

whyCool: A tiny change in the crowd can nearly double the rare events that matter.
caveat: The tail is heavily magnified and the rate model holds the barrier fixed; no fresh reaction application was tested.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
